name: Egglife Original Egg White Wraps
ingredients_found: Cage Free Egg Whites, Less than 2% of Xanthan Gum, Sea Salt, Natural Flavor, Nisin (Natural Preservative).
reason: Xanthan gum (L3 industrial gum/emulsifier); also carries the preservative nisin.
justification: Xanthan gum is an added industrial gum that acts as a surfactant on the intestinal mucin layer, stripping the mucosal shield and triggering an immediate L3 gut flag (Principle 1).
notes: Processed egg-white wrap, not whole eggs. Nisin is an added preservative on top of the L3 gum.

name: Three Little Pigs Uncured Bacon & Swiss Egg Bites
ingredients_found: Eggs, Swiss Cheese (Pasteurized Part-Skim Milk, Cheese Culture, Salt, Enzymes), Uncured Bacon (Pork, Water, Sea Salt, Less than 2% Natural Cane Sugar, Celery Powder, Spices), Cream, Sea Salt, Xanthan Gum, Garlic, Spices.
reason: Xanthan gum (L3 gum/emulsifier); also added cane sugar in the bacon (L2 hidden sugar in a savory staple).
justification: Added xanthan gum strips the mucosal barrier (Principle 1, L3), and the added cane sugar in a savory product drives hepatic lipogenesis (Principle 4, L2); either alone disqualifies.
notes: Sous-vide egg-bite convenience product, not whole eggs. Sold as 'Three Little Pigs' / Les Trois Petits Cochons.

name: Crack'd The No-Egg Egg (Plant-Based Egg Substitute)
ingredients_found: Water, Pea Protein (3%), Corn Oil, Thickener (Methyl Cellulose), Pea Starch, Gelling Agent (Gellan Gum), Flavourings, Firming Agent (Calcium Lactate), Dried Inactive Yeast, Acid (Lactic Acid), Black Salt, Acidity Regulator (Potassium Bitartrate), Colour (Beta Carotene), Stabilisers (Calcium Carbonate, Guar Gum, Cellulose Gum), Vitamins (D & B12), Dextrose.
reason: Corn oil (L3 industrial seed oil) plus multiple L3 gums (gellan gum, guar gum, cellulose gum, methylcellulose); also added dextrose (L2 sugar in a savory staple).
justification: Refined corn oil carries cytotoxic lipid hydroperoxides that hard-disqualify a savory staple (Principle 3, L3), and the stacked gums strip the mucosal barrier (Principle 1); an engineered pea-protein isolate is also a denatured, lower-bioavailability protein (Principle 2).
notes: Not an egg product at all (plant-based substitute). Ingredient deck is the UK/EU formula; the US retail version may vary slightly by region but plant-egg substitutes uniformly rely on seed oils + gelling gums. Disqualifies regardless.
